@graph.name: Field Notes
@graph.description: Short, practical notes on tracking equipment and the people who use it.

blogPost.headline: Who has the drill right now?
blogPost.description: The cheapest question to ask, and the most expensive to answer on the spot.

blogPost.headline: Where the 5 to 15 percent goes
blogPost.description: Nobody budgets for shrinkage. Everybody pays for it.

blogPost.headline: The spreadsheet that breaks at 200 assets
blogPost.description: Spreadsheets don't fail loudly. They quietly stop being true.

blogPost.headline: Chain of custody for equipment
blogPost.description: A signature on a paper hand receipt proves someone signed. It doesn't prove who has the radio today.

blogPost.headline: Serial number tracking, when spreadsheets stop working
blogPost.description: Counting how many you have is a different job from knowing which one is where.

blogPost.headline: Write-offs and loss tracking, done properly
blogPost.description: A missing row in a spreadsheet isn't a record that something is gone. It's the absence of one.

blogPost.headline: The coverage you forgot you had
blogPost.description: A warranty only pays out if you remember it exists at the moment something breaks.

blogPost.headline: Software that explains itself
blogPost.description: Help you have to catch is help you don’t have.

blogPost.headline: The button that says no
blogPost.description: A refusal you can read beats a success you cannot trust.

blogPost.headline: The shelf has a ceiling
blogPost.description: Why gear in someone’s hands still takes up room.

blogPost.headline: A column is not a question
blogPost.description: A column stores. A question means.
